# Security policy 🔒

## Supported version

Security fixes are applied to the latest code on the default branch and the
currently deployed application. Older commits, forks, and private deployments
are not maintained by this project.

## Report a vulnerability privately

> [!CAUTION]
> Do not include vulnerability details in a public issue, discussion, or pull
> request.

Prefer [GitHub Private Vulnerability Reporting](https://github.com/w04m1/elte-schedule-builder/security/advisories/new).
If that option is unavailable, email `w04m1@proton.me` with the subject
`ELTE Schedule Builder security report`.

Include:

- the affected page, endpoint, or commit;
- reproduction steps or a minimal proof of concept;
- the expected security impact;
- whether the issue affects the deployed site, local installations, or both;
- suggested remediation, if available.

Remove unrelated personal data, credentials, and real student schedules. Use
the local `DEMO-*` subjects whenever they can reproduce the problem.

## What to expect

The maintainer will aim to acknowledge a report within seven days, confirm the
scope, and coordinate remediation and disclosure. Complex reports may take
longer to investigate. Please allow a reasonable remediation period before
publishing details.

## Scope and safe testing

Good-faith testing of this project's own code and deployed application is
welcome when it avoids privacy violations, service disruption, and destructive
actions. Do not target ELTE, Tanrend, Google, Imgur, hosting providers, or other
third-party systems. Do not perform denial-of-service testing or access another
person's data.
